reasons: **We're right at the heat limit.** On the hottest part of the day, the crew is expected to get within a hair of the safe body-heat limit, with almost no room for error. If it turns out hotter than forecast, or someone is working harder than planned, stop and rest them right away.

**Kofi and Sam can't do the heaviest jobs in the heat.** Both are new to working in these conditions, so their bodies haven't adjusted yet. Give them lighter tasks during the hot hours, and save the hardest work for the rest of the crew or for cooler times.

**This plan gets more done, but with less safety cushion.** Doing the brush clearing in the cool morning gets about 82% of the important work finished. The other option, spreading the heat and afternoon breaks more evenly across everyone, keeps people a little cooler but only finishes about 70% of the work. Pick that one if you'd rather have more breathing room on heat.

Hard safety rules:
- Every worker's 90th percentile core temperature must stay below 38.0 °C all shift. Harder work, sun and high WBGT heat people up; 30-min shade rests cool them down.
- Breaks: at most 3 work slots in a row, then a 'rest' slot; at most 2 in a row if any of those slots has WBGT >= 30.0 °C.
- No outdoor tasks during hazards that stop outdoor work. After lightning, outdoor work stays stopped for 30 more minutes.
- Workers who are not acclimatized never do very_heavy tasks when WBGT >= 28.0 °C.
Validity: one entry per slot per worker; off-site workers rest; skills and allowed slots must match.
